title: Complete mechanism catalog from the AI Engineer transcript research
source_scope: Every supplied deep-read technique plus every takeaway from relevance >=3 talks not deep-read. Completeness is relative to these extraction inputs, not a claim that every possible idea in every subtitle was independently rediscovered in this consolidation.

methodology.loading: Python loaded all deep-read JSON records and all analysis JSON files; triage records were selected only for relevance >=3 and talk IDs absent from the deep-read set.
methodology.deduplication: Normalize Unicode/names, use mechanism-specific curated regex concepts and TF-IDF word/bigram cosine candidates, then manual semantic assignment and weak-match/outlier review. Abbreviations are word-bounded to avoid AST/fast, CLI/explicit and LoRA/exploration false matches. No top-N technique filter and no topic-count target were used.
methodology.mechanism_granularity: A cluster is one transferable intervention; variants and all source-specific changes remain in the cluster. Related but different interventions are kept separate. Source count means distinct talk IDs, not the number of extracted records.

classification_review.manual_conflict_resolution: Later curated assignments resolve earlier draft mappings; one final cluster per input record is enforced.

methodology.source_levels: A deep-read label means the supplied reader artifact was produced by a full-talk reader. This consolidation did not independently reread every talk in full. Triage-only ideas remain provisional even when merged beside a deep-read mechanism.
methodology.quotation: quote is a verbatim local-transcript excerpt (timestamp labels removed, line breaks retained), not a cleaned-up invented quotation. reported_quote and reported_timestamp preserve the extractor input. Normalized-exact and ordered-ellipsis matching locate words; fuzzy or claimed-time locations require confirmation. Eleven initially unresolved records were manually located in the original source. For six translated input quotes on an auto:hi phonetic-English ASR track, the original Devanagari excerpt is verbatim and the English input is explicitly labeled translated/paraphrased; ASR interpretation remains provisional. A matching quote does not prove its surrounding interpretation or performance claim.
methodology.numbers: Input counts and coverage are recomputed in Python. Speaker/reader measurement strings are preserved as reports, never used as independently verified local gains. Effort is an estimate; benefits are directional; overlapping savings must not be added.

verified: All current deep-read input files and every eligible triage takeaway accounted for exactly once or explicitly excluded
Cluster IDs, area lists, source counts, source levels, priority/ladder enums and effort ranges consistent
All retained and excluded records have original-transcript verbatim excerpts, timestamps and exact line-range equality
All analysis, deep-read input, transcript and baseline SHA-256 hashes match files on disk
Original technique names and reported quotes preserved; triage-only clusters remain C; existing-practice list is separate
remaining_limits: Dated implementation evidence is not a live production audit
Fuzzy locations, short quotes and phonetic-ASR interpretation are explicitly flagged for confirmation
Speaker/reader performance claims are reported evidence, not independently reproduced local gains

note: Identities are frozen; the generator must never write this file. reported_measurements are speaker/reader reports, not independently reproduced. Record counts describe the whole source catalog, including clusters not exported here.

sources.mechanism_in_source: With prompt caching, re-sent history is billed at the cached rate. Any compaction or summary, or clearing old tool outputs, rewrites the prefix. techniques.title: Convert repeatable conventions into lint, tests and governed rule assets

mechanism.summary: Convert repeatable conventions into lint, tests and governed rule assets
mechanism.representative_explanation: Agents have no memory and repeat the same elementary mistakes, and compaction erases corrections. Writing a linter is now cheap because the agent writes it. So, on a schedule, mine past transcripts and review comments for repeated feedback and codify the deterministic ones as lint rules, e.g. design-system component use, OpenAPI decorators, or skill code blocks that must type-check. Expect whack-a-mole: the agent first dodged the rule by deleting the code blocks, then the backticks.

techniques.title: Bind sensitive side effects to exact validated payload and current state

mechanism.summary: Bind sensitive side effects to exact validated payload and current state
mechanism.representative_explanation: Deterministic code owns control flow, evidence and side effects. Each external action has its own gate, and its approval is tied to the hash of the exact payload and re-checked right before execution. Side effects move through prepared → sent → completed. An unknown outcome goes to manual review, never to an automatic retry. Follow-ups run as new child plans (at most 5 rounds); the approved parent never changes. Wait expiry (default 72 h) is decided by a rule, not a model.

sources.talk: We let an AI agent execute Bash and lived to talk about it (Sarah Sanders, PostHog)
sources.quote:
because at Post Hog we build everything in the open and they inject something in
a markdown file or a seemingly harmless code comment and we have some sort of
like LLM powered code review going through that and it says looks good to
me and ignores it. We may have just shipped a prompt injection payload
sources.input_technique: Deterministic scan of everything injected into agent context, at the source and again at the point of use
sources.mechanism_in_source: Docs, skills and example code that agents load form a supply chain. A poisoned markdown file or code comment in an open-source PR can pass an LLM code review, and then it ships into every agent run. PostHog scans that content with deterministic YARA rules twice: when it is built or released, and again when it is loaded. Each rule matches a verb together with an instruction-like noun (not the verb alone), ships with negative tests, and gets a severity based on real impact. Enforcement is purely mechanical. An optional LLM triage step may only remove noise from findings that did not block, and it fails closed.

Agents already do most of their work through bash. Exposing a library or CLI (and letting code filter or aggregate the result) replaces dozens of tool definitions and large JSON dumps.

sources.input_technique: Count the maintenance cost of a fine-tuned model before choosing it
sources.mechanism_in_source: Their fine-tuned small intent classifier paid off, but every defect fix meant collecting examples, generating synthetic ones, labelling by hand and retraining, about a week each time. Fixes caused regressions on old cases (whack-a-mole), and the team got locked into one base model. They moved the behaviour into editable prompts and skills, checked each change against a curated regression set from production, and cut fix time to under an hour. Cost per message went up, but total cost went down.
